captions.detailed: A Napoleonic-era wheeled field cannon with a two-wheel wooden carriage and a cast smooth-bore barrel. The main body consists of a dark olive-green carriage with a long trailing trail, supporting a bronze-colored smooth-bore barrel. The barrel has a tapered design with a cascabel at the rear and rests on trunnions at the carriage cheeks. Two large brown wooden wheels with dark rims and spokes are mounted on a central transverse axle, allowing continuous rotation. The barrel elevates on a revolute joint about its trunnion axis, while a quoin wedge beneath the breech slides prismatically along the carriage bed to adjust elevation.
captions.instruction: Generate a Napoleonic-era wheeled field cannon as an articulated object. The assembly should feature a dark olive-green carriage, two large spoked wooden wheels rotating continuously on their axle, a bronze-colored smooth-bore barrel that elevates via a revolute joint on its trunnions, and an elevation quoin wedge that slides prismatically along the carriage bed.
captions.factory: Construct the main chassis (carriage) using box primitives for the trail and cheeks, and a cylinder for the axle. Model the smooth-bore barrel using a series of lofts or tapered cylinders, adding cylinders for the trunnions and a sphere for the cascabel. Create the spoked wheels by combining a central cylinder for the hub, a thin outer ring for the rim, and multiple rotated cylinder spokes. Assemble the parts using joints: define continuous joints for the two wheels relative to the axle, a revolute joint for the barrel's elevation about the trunnion axis, and a prismatic joint for the quoin wedge sliding along the carriage bed.
